findings.title: Phone line form: the Total cost box rewrites itself on every keystroke, so you can't type a lot total into it
findings.evidence: value={line.qty * line.unitCost ? (line.qty * line.unitCost).toFixed(2) : ''} with onChange: const newTotal = parseFloat(e.target.value); if (!Number.isFinite(newTotal) || line.qty <= 0) return; const unit = +(newTotal / line.qty).toFixed(2); set('unitCost', unit). The input has no raw-text state of its own (unlike qtyRaw/costRaw). Its value is always derived as qty*unit formatted to 2 decimals. React 18's number-input update (react-dom ReactDOMInput: `node.value != value` with value the string '1.00') writes '1.00' back over the typed '1'. Desktop LineDrawer.tsx:680 avoids this by keeping the typed string in line.totalCost.
findings.failure_scenario: Qty 1, the purchaser starts typing 150 in Total cost. After '1' the box shows '1.00'. Typing '5' makes '1.005', which parses to unit 1.00 and shows '1.00' again, so the value stays at $1. With qty 3, '1' shows as '0.99' (unit 0.33). Backspace to empty parses as NaN and returns early, so the box can't be cleared either. The comment above the row says this field exists so a purchaser 'can enter the negotiated bulk total', and on the phone that only works by pasting.
findings.proposed_fix: Mirror the desktop drawer: keep a totalRaw string state that the input renders while it is being edited. Derive unitCost from it, and clear totalRaw when qty or unit cost is edited.
findings.regression_test: RTL test on SubmitForm. Type qty 3, then type '1','0','0' into Total cost. Expect the box to read '100' and unit cost '33.33'.

findings.title: Double-tapping Add item when adding a line from an existing PO's products screen inserts the line twice
findings.evidence: The Save button is <button className="ph-btn dark" onClick={() => attemptSave()}> with no busy/disabled prop. attemptSave goes straight to persist(typed) → onSaveLine. In MobileApp.onSaveLine with backToDetail (returnTo==='detail' && editingId), the capture stays in phase 'form' until the PATCH lands ('Hold the form until it lands'). A second tap therefore passes the `capture.phase !== 'form'` guard and enqueues a second write. A new line has no id, so each write sends api.patch('/api/orders/'+targetId, { addLines: [toAddLine(line)] }).
findings.failure_scenario: A purchaser on slow dock Wi-Fi adds a RAM line (qty 10) to an existing PO from the products screen and taps Add item twice. Two addLines PATCHes run back to back through the write queue. The PO now has two identical lines (20 units of phantom stock, double the cost), and the second may also re-flush the buffered photos.
findings.proposed_fix: Pass a `saving` prop into SubmitForm (pendingWrites > 0, or a local latch set in onSaveLine for the backToDetail path) and disable the Save and pnGen 'Use' buttons while it is set. Or have onSaveLine refuse a second call for the same line._cid while one is in flight.
findings.regression_test: MobileApp test: open the line form from an existing order's products screen, mock api.patch with a deferred promise, click Save twice, and assert api.patch was called once with addLines.

findings.title: [cross-lane] fmtDate/fmtDateShort render calendar dates as UTC instants: Home follow-up dates and package ETAs show the previous day in Denver
findings.evidence: format.ts: `export const fmtDateShort = (d: Date | string, locale = 'en-US') => new Date(d).toLocaleDateString(locale, { month: 'short', day: 'numeric' });` (no timeZone). routes/home.ts:85 sends `to_char(s.next_follow_up_at, 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS next_follow_up_at`, and DesktopHome.tsx:125 prints `fmtDateShort(f.nextFollowUpAt, locale)`. new Date('2026-11-03') is UTC midnight, which is Nov 2 17:00 MDT. Package ETAs (packages.tracking_eta TIMESTAMPTZ, home.ts:63) arrive as '...T00:00:00.000Z' calendar dates; DesktopHome.tsx:153/356 and Home.tsx:195 pass them to fmtDateShort too. lib/shippingList.ts:22-33 fmtEta already knows about this ('a date-only value (or its UTC-midnight round trip through the DB) rendered in a western timezone would show the previous day') and pins timeZone:'UTC', but the Home cards bypass it. | Pages-reviewer confirmation: return o.package.eta ? t('homeEta', { date: fmtDateShort(o.package.eta, locale) }) : ... fmtDateShort is new Date(d).toLocaleDateString(locale, { month:'short', day:'numeric' }) with no timeZone. Backend shipping/types.ts parseEta stores a date-only carrier ETA ('2026-11-03') as UTC midnight in the TIMESTAMPTZ tracking_eta. home.ts:63 returns it as pkg_eta. lib/shippingList.ts fmtEta exists for exactly this reason: it detects the UTC-midnight shape and formats with timeZone:'UTC'.
findings.failure_scenario: A supplier's follow-up falls due tomorrow, 2026-11-03 (daysUntil=1). In Denver the Home 'Follow-ups' row reads 'Nov 2', which is today, while the row is not styled as due today. A package with ETA 2026-11-05T00:00:00Z reads 'ETA Nov 4' on Home and 'Thu, Nov 5' on the Shipping page.
findings.proposed_fix: Format calendar dates with timeZone:'UTC', either with a fmtCalendarDate helper (the same idea as accounting.ts fmtBookDay) for date-only/UTC-midnight values, or by sending ETAs on Home through fmtEta. Switch DesktopHome.tsx:125/153/356 and Home.tsx:195 to it.
findings.regression_test: With process.env.TZ='America/Denver' (or vi.useFakeTimers plus a TZ-pinned run), assert that the helper renders '2026-11-03' as 'Nov 3' and '2026-11-05T00:00:00.000Z' as 'Nov 5'.

findings.title: Inventory editor: clearing the Unit cost field saves the lot at $0 cost
findings.evidence: `if (Number(draft.unitCost) !== Number(initial.unitCost)) patch.unitCost = Number(draft.unitCost) || 0;` Number('') is 0, so a blanked field counts as a change to 0 and is sent as unitCost:0. The caller DesktopInventoryEdit.tsx:288 sends this patch. Save is disabled only on `!dirty || saving || archived` (line 351). The backend validateLineInput (apps/backend/src/lib/orderInput.ts:44) accepts 0 ('unitCost must be a number of 0 or more'), so the write goes through. (A blanked qty becomes 0 too, but the server rejects that with 400, so it is not silent.)
findings.failure_scenario: A manager selects the unit cost '19' to retype it, gets distracted and clicks Save with the field empty. The lot's unit_cost becomes 0, which feeds inventory value, profit and commission ((unit_price - unit_cost) * qty) with no warning.
findings.proposed_fix: Treat a blank unit cost as 'no change' (skip the key) or as a validation error, and block Save with a message. Never coerce '' to 0. Do the same for qty instead of relying on the server's 400.
findings.regression_test: inventoryEditPatch(base, { ...base, unitCost: '' }) should not contain unitCost: 0. Expect either {} or a thrown/flagged validation error, depending on the chosen fix.

findings.title: [cross-lane] Review/Commission-tab commission preview disagrees with the commission the backend owes (unpriced lines' cost charged, negative not clamped)
findings.evidence: reviewMoney: `const profit = revenue - cost.total; const commission = profit * rate; earns: (selfReimbursed ? cost.total : 0) + commission` where revenue counts only priced lines but cost.total is the WHOLE PO's goods + fees (poEffectiveCost over every line). The backend's figure for the same commission everywhere it is used (bank picker routes/bankTx.ts:1263, accounting commission lens routes/accounting.ts:292, home.ts:40/200, services/poRealized.ts:49) is `GREATEST(rz.projected_profit,0) * commission_rate`, with projected_profit from lib/po-cost.ts:121-123 = SUM((sell_price - effUnitCost) * qty) over lines — an unpriced line (sell_price NULL) drops out of the SUM entirely, and a negative projection is clamped to 0. The poRealized.ts header comment states this is deliberate ('an unpriced line contributes nothing — neither its revenue nor its cost ... clamped at zero').
findings.failure_scenario: PO with lines A 4x$10 sold @$25, B 2x$30 unpriced, C 1x$5 @$8, fees $7, rate 50% (the reviewPricing test fixture). Box Check / Commission tab shows profit -$4, commission -$2, 'earns' -$2 (red). Backend: projected_profit = priced lines only, roughly (25-10)*4+(8-5) minus their fee share ≈ +$56, commission ≈ $28; that is what the bank-link picker matches against and what Accounting/Home report as owed. Likewise any fully priced PO below cost shows a negative commission the server treats as $0. The manager approving on the Review page sees a different payout than the system books.
findings.proposed_fix: Compute the preview on the backend's basis: commission = max(0, Σ_priced qty*(sell − effUnitCost)) * rate, with effUnitCost spreading the lot price/fees the way po-cost.ts effUnitCost does — or have the server return projected_profit/commission on GET and render that. If the all-in figure is intentionally different, label it and also show the owed amount.
findings.regression_test: reviewPricing.test.ts: with an unpriced line and with revenue < cost, assert reviewMoney().commission equals the backend's clamped per-line formula (pin both sides against a shared fixture or a shared helper in packages/shared).

findings.title: Phone PO list silently stops at 30 rows while the header counts all of them
findings.evidence: The effect walks every keyset page ('The list filters and counts client-side, so it holds every PO in scope'). The header says t('ordersSubmitted', { n: visibleOrders.length }), but the render is filtered.slice(0, 30) with no 'show more' and no hint.
findings.failure_scenario: A manager with 85 non-Done POs sees '85 orders' and 30 cards. PO #31 onward can only be reached by searching its id. Market.tsx was fixed for the same 'quietly cut to 30' issue, but this list wasn't.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a 'Load more' / incremental reveal, or at least a 'Showing 30 of N, search to narrow' line.
findings.regression_test: Render Orders with 40 mocked summaries. Assert 40 rows can be reached, or that a 'show more' control appears.

findings.title: Mark Done can be fired twice during the commission-evidence check, and the second ends in a misleading 'stage moved' error
findings.evidence: canAdvance = !!nextStatus && !advancing && !saving, but advance() only sets advancing inside doAdvance. Before that it awaits takeover.ask(order), which 'resolves at once when there is nothing to ask' (ManagerTakeoverDialog.tsx:19), and then `await commissionPayments.check()`, which is a network read. The button stays enabled for that whole round trip.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner-manager taps 'Mark Done' twice on a PO whose commission is already linked to a payment. Both taps pass check() and both call doAdvance with fromStage 'ready_to_pay'. The first moves the PO to Done. The second gets the server's stage-moved refusal and shows the 'PO moved to Done, reload' error dialog over a successful action. The fromStage guard prevents any data harm.
findings.proposed_fix: Set advancing (or a ref latch) at the top of advance() and clear it on every early return.
findings.regression_test: Render OrderDetail at Ready to Pay as a manager with commissionPayments.check deferred. Click Mark Done twice and assert one POST /advance.

findings.title: RMB card prefills the full sale total again once a CNY sale is fully (or over-) paid
findings.evidence: AccountingCard passes `...(owed > 0 ? { amount: owed } : {})`, so with owed <= 0 the preset has no amount. initialForm then uses `(preset?.amount ?? preset?.target?.amount) ? Number(...).toFixed(2) : ''`, which falls through to target.amount, the sell order's whole total (findTargets 'so' amount). orderAmount() also uses the full total because orderAmountOverride is undefined.
findings.failure_scenario: A CNY sell order with total ¥10,000 already has ¥10,000 booked. Clicking 'Record' opens the form prefilled with 10000.00 and amountSource 'order', which invites a duplicate receipt. After a partial payment the card correctly offers the remainder, so the full-total prefill shows up only in the paid-off state.
findings.proposed_fix: In AccountingCard pass `amount: Math.max(owed, 0)` for CNY sales, and have initialForm distinguish 'preset amount 0' from 'no preset' (use `preset.amount !== undefined`), leaving the field blank when nothing is owed.
findings.regression_test: initialForm({ preset: { kind: 'sale', amount: 0, target: { id: 'SO-1', amount: 100, currency: 'CNY' } } }).amount === ''.

findings.title: Frontend vitest has no pinned TZ, so CI (UTC runners) can't catch the timezone regressions the tests claim to guard
findings.evidence: The test comment says 'its UTC-midnight round trip must not slip to the previous day in a western timezone', but neither the vitest config, package.json nor the workflow sets TZ, and ubuntu-latest runs in UTC. In UTC, new Date('2026-09-22T00:00:00.000Z').toLocaleDateString() is Sep 22 with or without the timeZone:'UTC' fix, so the assertion passes even if fmtEta's fix is removed. For the same reason no test can catch the fmtDateShort finding above.
findings.failure_scenario: Someone deletes the `...(dateOnly ? { timeZone: 'UTC' } : {})` line in shippingList.fmtEta. CI stays green and Denver users see every ETA a day early.
findings.proposed_fix: Set TZ for the frontend test run, e.g. `"test": "TZ=America/Denver vitest run"` or `process.env.TZ = 'America/Denver'` in a vitest globalSetup, so the date tests run in the business's own timezone.
findings.regression_test: After pinning, temporarily remove the timeZone:'UTC' branch in fmtEta and confirm the trackingNote test fails.

findings.title: Add-package form fills a below-floor PayPal id (and wipes a typed one) while telling the user no id was found
findings.evidence: `setPaypalTxnIdState(scan.txnId ?? '')` runs unconditionally, then `else if (scan.txnId === null || scan.confidence < AI_UNREADABLE_FLOOR) setScanNoticeKey('shipPayNoTxnFound')`. The shared rule readPaypalScan (paypalTxn.ts:20-28, 'One rule for the cost payment and the commission payment, so the two cannot disagree') returns txnId null below AI_UNREADABLE_FLOOR and is used by usePaymentProof, but this form re-implements it without that drop and without normalizing. Backend /api/scan/payment (routes/scan.ts:275-282) returns the raw read and confidence, so nothing upstream filters it.
findings.failure_scenario: Purchaser types the correct id, then drops a blurry screenshot: scan returns txnId 'XXXXXXXXXXXX' at confidence 0.15 -> typed id is replaced by the garbage read, banner says 'no transaction id found', and the required-id check passes so the package is saved with the wrong id, which banktx auto-linking later keys on. A read of null likewise wipes the typed id.
findings.proposed_fix: Use readPaypalScan(scan): only set the txn id when read.txnId is non-null, and set the notice from read.noticeKey.
findings.regression_test: Extract the scan->state mapping into a pure helper (or reuse readPaypalScan) and test that confidence < AI_UNREADABLE_FLOOR or txnId null leaves the existing id untouched.

findings.title: Chip auto-fill for an intermediate part # survives when the part # is changed back to the one the line opened with
findings.evidence: chipFillQuery returns '' when `canon === mem.mountPart`, so no lookup runs and the `else if (mem.current.autoFilled !== null) onFill('')` cleanup path is never reached; autoFilled stays set because the chip still equals it.
findings.failure_scenario: Line opened with part A and blank chip. User edits part to B (>=6 chars, 300 ms pause) -> chip auto-filled with B's chip. User reverts the part # to A -> no query, B's chip stays on line A. chip_number is a material field, so the save stores a wrong chip # (and a purchaser's submitted PO reverts to Draft for it).
findings.proposed_fix: When q is '' because canon === mountPart (or too short) and mem.autoFilled is non-null, clear the hook's own fill (onFill('') and autoFilled = null), mirroring the no-answer branch.
findings.regression_test: Needs a renderer; or factor the 'should clear own fill' decision into a pure function next to chipFillQuery and test mountPart revert with autoFilled set.

findings.title: Price-sheet precheck misses headers the backend parser accepts (formula/str cells, prefixed SpreadsheetML), refusing a valid file client-side
findings.evidence: Headers are only read from `<t>` elements (`/<t(?:\s[^>]*)?>([^<]*)<\/t>/`) and rows counted with `/<row[\s>]/`. A header produced by a formula is stored as `<c t="str"><f>..</f><v>Part Number</v></c>` (no <t>), and workbooks written by OpenXML-SDK-style exporters use a namespace prefix (`<x:row>`, `<x:t>`). The backend (services/priceSheet.ts cellText) reads formula results and any XML form via ExcelJS, so these files parse server-side, but the precheck returns columns-missing/no-rows and the upload is refused before reaching the authoritative parser.
findings.failure_scenario: Vendor sheet whose header row is `="Part Number"` or whose XML is `<x:sheetData><x:row>...<x:is><x:t>Unit Price</x:t>` -> precheck says 'Part Number / Unit Price columns not found' although the backend would import it.
findings.proposed_fix: Also collect `<v>` text of t="str"/"inlineStr" cells and allow an optional namespace prefix (`<(?:\w+:)?t\b`, `<(?:\w+:)?row\b`); or, on a columns-missing precheck, let the upload proceed and rely on the server's verdict.
findings.regression_test: priceFilePrecheck.test.ts: storedZip with `<c t="str"><v>Part Number</v></c>` and with x:-prefixed sheet/sharedStrings -> expect ok.

findings.title: Chunk-reload recovery dies when the sessionStorage accessor itself throws
findings.evidence: `if (shouldReload(window.sessionStorage, Date.now()))` evaluates `window.sessionStorage` outside shouldReload's try/catch. shouldReload (lines 32-46) only guards store.getItem/setItem. In Chrome/Safari with site data blocked, reading the `window.sessionStorage` property throws SecurityError itself, so the listener throws before shouldReload runs. The comment at 36-37 ('Storage can throw outright... one wasted reload beats a dead page') describes exactly this case, but only the method-throws variant is handled. chunkReload.test.ts:56 ('reloads when storage throws') passes a store whose methods throw, so it would pass with this bug.
findings.failure_scenario: A browser that blocks site storage keeps a tab open across a deploy. The next lazy() import fails, and vite:preloadError fires. Reading window.sessionStorage throws SecurityError inside the listener, so there is no reload and the user is left on the ErrorBoundary or skeleton, not the one automatic reload the module promises.
findings.proposed_fix: Resolve the store lazily inside a try: `let store; try { store = window.sessionStorage; } catch { store = { getItem: () => null, setItem: () => {} }; }`. Or have shouldReload take a getter and call it inside its existing try.
findings.regression_test: Make installChunkReload testable with an injected window, or export a `storeOrNull()` helper. Assert that a window whose `sessionStorage` getter throws still calls location.reload() once.

findings.title: Timing beacon reports loadEvent=0 when the tab is hidden before `load`, skewing the slow-load stream toward zero
findings.evidence: installTiming reports on the first `visibilitychange` to hidden, even before `load` has fired. In report(), `loadEvent: Math.round(nav.loadEventEnd - nav.startTime)` (line 50) is 0 because loadEventEnd stays 0 until load completes. Then `sent = true` blocks the real report. The backend (routes/clientTimings.ts:57-61) accepts 0 as a valid loadEvent and logs it.
findings.failure_scenario: On a slow cold load (say 8 s), the user switches tabs at 3 s. The report goes out with loadEvent 0 and lcp null or partial, and is recorded as a 0 ms load. The loads the stream exists to measure (slow cold loads where people tab away) become the fastest data points.
findings.proposed_fix: In report(), return early without setting `sent` when `nav.loadEventEnd === 0`, so a later trigger can report. Or send loadEvent: null with an `incomplete: true` flag and have the backend reject or segregate those reports.
findings.regression_test: Stub performance.getEntriesByType to return {loadEventEnd: 0, ...}, fire visibilitychange hidden, and assert that no beacon was sent (or that it was flagged). Then set loadEventEnd and fire load+5s, and assert the real numbers are sent.

findings.title: Reddit lead detail for a seller named `buyers` or `attention` hits the static route instead
findings.evidence: `detail: (u) => api.get(`${BASE}/${key(u)}`)` sends GET /api/leads/reddit/<username>. The backend (routes/redditLeads.ts:134,143,176) registers GET '/attention' and GET '/buyers' before GET '/:username', and encodeURIComponent leaves those names unchanged.
findings.failure_scenario: A harvested seller u/buyers or u/attention (both valid Reddit usernames) is opened in Leads ▸ Reddit. The client gets {buyers:[...]} or {n} where it expects {lead, history, buyers}, so the detail drawer crashes or renders blank. Claim, release and the other writes work, because they use /:username/<verb>.
findings.proposed_fix: Move the collection routes under a non-username namespace, such as /api/leads/reddit/_/buyers and /_/attention (underscore-led names that Reddit allows but the harvest can reject), or move lead detail to /api/leads/reddit/u/:username.
findings.regression_test: Backend route test: seed a lead with username 'buyers' and assert that GET /api/leads/reddit/buyers via the detail path returns {lead.username:'buyers'}.

carryover.evidence: apps/frontend/src/pages/Inventory.tsx:70-76 pages through /api/inventory with limit=200 and nextCursor via forEachKeysetPage.
tests/orderSubmit.test.ts asserts removeLineIds/addLines/noop branches; the MobileApp queue side belongs to another lane.

notes: Lane split across four sub-reviewers plus the lead; every listed file was read in full except the CSS files (desktop/facebookPool/fleet/phone/tokens/accounting/onboarding/redditLeads.css) and the i18n tables (i18n.tsx, i18n.zh.ts), which were skimmed (countKey/t() fallback read; en/zh singular parity checked: all 63 *One keys present in zh). No production files changed; no repro tests kept. Not verified in a browser; none of the shared pages have component tests, so UI findings rest on code reading (React number-input write-back confirmed in react-dom source). Sub-reviewer notes: Authorize.tsx: no defect found. redirectUri always comes from the backend's pending row, which was matched against the client's registered URIs at /oauth/authorize, and DCR and manager registration both run isValidRedirectUri (rejects javascript:/data:). state is carried server-side. Consent and deny go through rawFetch, which adds the X-Requested-By CSRF header, behind authMiddleware. One minor gap: rawFetch does no 401 refresh, so approving after the access cookie expires on an idle consent page shows a bare 'unauthorized' instead of refreshing. Not reported. Login.tsx: the redirect after login is handled by readSafeNext in DesktopApp/MobileApp (it rejects //, /\, and cross-origin). Errors are shown. There is no <form>, so Enter/'Go' does not submit. That is UX, not reported. OrderDetail save/advance/confirmCommission: refetch-after-write and draft-version invalidation look right. A failed save keeps the draft, and the commission sheet refetches when a write landed before a failed move. Shipping.tsx: the scan lookup is seq-guarded, createPo has busy guards, and AddPackageScreen's Enter path goes through useAddPackageForm's canSubmit and submitting latch. Not verified by running anything. No component tests exist for these pages. I checked React 18's number-input update logic in node_modules/react-dom to confirm the SubmitForm finding. Read every file in the list in full (source and tests). Compared each client call with the backend: coordinator.ts (all coordinatorApi paths are served, and the settings body only sends keys inside SEARCH_SETTING_FIELDS; date_listed scalar-vs-list is handled by rs_console settings.py:438); tracker.ts (every trackerApi path is on the allowlist); fleet.ts and its sub-routers (workers, slots, hosts, releases, proxies, proxyHealth all exist; city-log hour caps are respected); facebookPool.ts routes; wechatMarket.ts (params kind/key/side/until/days match); redditLeads.ts. lib/api.ts throws ApiError on every non-2xx and parses error bodies safely, so I found no client helper that treats an error as success. Ids are encodeURIComponent'd everywhere that matters; the unencoded ones are system ids (PO-/SO-, numeric account no, uuids). route.ts navigate/guard logic held up against the evented-window tests. I could not find a reachable unencoded id that would let a browser-normalized hash leak selfNavs. Dropped after verification: an aiReview orderId race (DesktopBoxCheck is keyed by order id), a useMarketLookup out-of-order race (seq guard is correct), buildVersion/chunkReload loops (bounded by the 60 s guard and the `stale` latch), and beacon `established` surviving logout (already-reported class). Minor drift not reported: backend WORKER_ID refuses '.' while VNC_WORKER_ID allows it, so /workers/:id/logins|cities|queue would 400 for a dotted coordinator worker id. I could not confirm that such ids exist. Checked and found sound: convertAmount/previewCny FX direction (rate = CNY per USD; USD->CNY multiplies, CNY->USD divides) and rounding to the fen; toRequestBody's amount/rate bounds; splitYuan's -0.00 handling; fmtBookDay (UTC-pinned); localToday/phonePeriod (shared date helpers); owedOnSale (ledgerFor already excludes voided entries); paymentGap's cent-integer comparison; fxRate's inversion; carriers.ts regexes (the 1Z/UPS, EC..US, 12/15-digit FedEx and 20-22-digit 9-prefix USPS rules overlap only on the documented 96-prefix ambiguity; the IMpb ZIP9-then-ZIP5 strip can't yield a false USPS on standard 20/22-digit numbers; 26/34-digit IMpb numbers simply aren't detected and fall to the manual carrier pick); keywordRules parser/precedence/literal fallback; boxCheck scan matching; orderLookback last-match logic; handoff blockers; linePhotos buffer (failed uploads stay queued); archiveConflict. I could not check that keywordRules matches the Python monitor (ai_marketplace_monitor/utils.py is_substring) because the vendored monitor source isn't in this checkout. Tests in the list mostly assert real behaviour. accountingForm/keywordRules/boxCheck/handoff/linePhotos tests are strong, inventoryGroupSort.test and materialEdit.test exercise @recycle-erp/shared rather than lib code, and inventoryEditPatch.test lacks a blank-field case. Minor items not reported: fmtUSD(-0.004) renders '-$0.00'; lineRequirements accepts fractional qty that the server then 400s; the orderLookback 'done' stage lists Done notes/files from every pass, not only the latest. Read every listed file in full. useLineSaveQueue.ts itself is not in the list (only its test); the test looked meaningful. poPermissions: canEditOrder/canDelete ignore ownership, but backend detail/patch/delete all 403 a non-owner purchaser (routes/orders/detail.ts:71, patch.ts:116,352, lifecycle.ts:84) and closed-book/archived edits are refused in patch.ts, so no over-permission. poReadiness local vs server blocker sets checked (collector/carrier fold into server missingDelivery/missingTracking) — OK. readStoredGoodsTotal vs reviewMoney's local lot-price check use different epsilon forms (|d|<0.01 vs cent rounding) but stored values are NUMERIC(12,2), so they agree in practice. parsePriceInput accepts '1e3'/'0x10' (Number semantics) — judged too narrow to report. status.ts comment says floors are kept in sync with backend CONFIDENCE_FLOOR, which no longer exists in apps/backend (stale comment only). useAccountingTarget/useCommissionPayments keep the previous record's data across an id change with silent failures; not reported because I did not confirm a caller that reuses the instance across ids. sheetImage.ts canvas math not exercised.
